messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran an nsys + perfetto sweep on the INT8 serving path after the rollback yesterday. Seeing a big regression tied to per-layer dequant kernels and frequent HtoD host copies.

maria: TL;DR: dequantize_kernel and copy_htod_async dominate sample time for short sequences; overall 18% tail latency increase on 8k RPS test.

maria: nsys command I ran:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=nsys/int8-dequant-sweep \
  --sampling-frequency=1000 --cpuctxsw --sample=none --duration=60 \
  -- ./bin/serve --model gptq-int8 --batcher-config samples/short-seq.json
```

maria: quick parsed results (from the timeline/flame):
- dequantize_kernel: 34.7% GPU time (many small kernels, ~6-12us each)
- fused_gemm_attn: 27.1% GPU time
- kv_cache_read: ~6.2% but shows many small launches
- copy_htod_async spikes aligned with dequant bursts (~12-15ms windows)

sam: is the dequant done as a separate op per layer? seems like fusion should help.

jon: yep, current graph does per-layer dequant right now because we materialize int8->fp16 before attention. leads to many launches and host transfers for spilled buffers.

anya: can you paste a short perfetto timeline snippet / screenshot link? i want to see overlaps.

perf-bot: Uploaded perfetto trace: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcdef1234 (artifact stored at artifacts/nsys/1782345678/perfetto.pb)

maria: pasted short nvprof-like samples from nsys report:
```
Kernel                         Calls  Total GPU Time  Avg (us)
----------------------------------------------------------
dequantize_kernel               1843     0.622s       337.6
fused_gemm_attn                 412      0.485s       1176.6
copy_htod_async                 56       0.210s       3750.0
```

kevin: 3 things to try quickly:
1) fuse dequant into attention kernel (in-place) to avoid materializing
2) pre-dequant whole sequence in one batched kernel (reduce calls)
3) try keeping dequant on GPU and avoid host copies (was there an H2D fallback?)

sam: also check occupancy for dequant kernel — if it's tiny it could be launch overhead bound.

jon: i profiled occupancy: dequant kernels have low SM utilization but high number of kernel launches; occupancy ~12% for small seq lengths.

anya: how much does quantization speedup degrade when we fuse? worried about accuracy drift, need evals.

maria: accuracy delta is negligible on our short eval set for in-place fused dequant (0.1% ppl change). but need wider eval.

kevin: can we add a switch to runtime to prefer fused path for seq_len <= 32 and fallback for long sequences? simple heuristic.

maria: good idea. will prototype runtime flag: QUANT_FUSE_SHORT_SEQ=true and run microbench.

sam: also consider caching dequantized prefix in KV cache so repeated prefixes don't re-dequantize.

jon: note: current KV layout stores values in fp16 when model loaded, so dequant at runtime happens on hot path per request for newly produced tokens — caching helps only if prefixes repeat.

maria: next steps I will take:
- build branch with in-place fused dequant kernel + runtime flag
- run targeted microbench (seq=8,16,32) and full RPS test
- run accuracy eval against 2k prompts
- upload new nsys/perfetto traces for comparison

anya: add a small reproducer script so we can run perf on dev GPUs

maria: yep — pushing a minimal reproducer to PR in 10m with instructions. cc @kevin @jon for review :shipit:

kevin: if patch looks good, we can A/B rollout to dedicated pool before flipping globally.

maria: one more note — saw a weird host-side stall at 3:41:12 where CUDA stream sync aligned with Python GC spike (maybe slow code path causing batching delays). putting a GC.disable around the test changed tail by ~2%.

sam: interesting — please capture that in the perf notes, could be runtime batching heuristic interaction.

maria: will. uploading artifacts and linking in the PR.

perf-bot: Artifact bundle: s3://redwood-artifacts/perf/1782345678-int8-dequant-sweep.tar.gz

maria: thanks all. any quick objections before I open the draft PR?

jon: no objections, good plan.

anya: nope — go ahead.

kevin: go for it. :+1:
